target_customer: Mid-market and enterprise ecommerce teams and agencies building headless storefronts
problem: Headless commerce teams must stitch together backends, CMS and search and build the frontend from scratch. Alokai (formerly Vue Storefront) supplies an open-source frontend framework and a managed platform.
business_model: open-source core with enterprise subscription for managed frontend platform (frontend as a service)

founders.name: Patrick Friday
founders.background_notes: About 10 years of B2B sales and marketing per YC page.

founders.name: Filip Rakowski
founders.background_notes: Started programming at 13 per YC page.

founders.name: Bart Roszkowski
founders.background_notes: YC page claims three exits including Vue Storefront; company-stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: A frontend framework with an integration layer across many commerce backends is standard engineering with hard parts in maintaining many connectors.

defensibility.rationale: Open source adoption and a partner ecosystem (commercetools, SAP, Salesforce, BigCommerce) create integration lock-in, but frameworks like Next.js are free alternatives.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Platform vendors shipped their own frontends, but Alokai kept raising and remained independent through 2026.

market_need_then: Headless and composable commerce was growing in 2020 and 2021, with Series A text citing a wave of well-funded backend module vendors that left the frontend unserved.

branding.name_origin: Alokai is from the Hawaiian Alakai, meaning leader or guide, with the a changed to an o to signal openness; evokes a conductor leading an orchestra (company rebrand announcement, March 2024). The earlier name Vue Storefront was descriptive.
branding.domain_note: alokai.com adopted at the March 2024 rebrand; the previous brand used vuestorefront.io.

identity.logo: new logo reflecting connectivity and agnosticism

branding.brand_signature: Vue Storefront open-source community with Discord server

rebrands.why: Name no longer fit after the React version in March 2023 and broader product scope.

branding.community_and_virality: Large open-source developer community (10,000 plus developers per YC page) and Discord.

brand_strength.rationale: Vue Storefront was well known among headless commerce developers and ranked as a top ecommerce frontend framework on GitHub per company; the rename was a deliberate reset.

pivots.to: framework-agnostic frontend as a service (React support added)
pivots.why: Broaden to enterprise ecommerce teams; the name was later changed to match.

outcome_analysis: Alokai rode the headless commerce shift, with open-source adoption driving pipeline and a partner ecosystem driving enterprise deals. It raised a seed in January 2021, a $17.4M Series A in October 2021 and a $20M extension in March 2023, then rebranded in March 2024 and moved toward enterprise licensing. It remains active with 100 plus staff and no exit.
notes: The company's own Series A post carries a date of 22 Feb 2022 while tech.eu dated the round 13 Oct 2021; tech.eu date used. Sources disagree on 2023 round (company says $20M equity; Sifted reports 20 million euros). The 2023 round URL was seen only in search results and not opened. Competitors: the two articles opened (company post, tech.eu) name none, only partners; searches returned only post-2023 comparisons of Next.js Commerce, Hydrogen and PWA Studio, so the list is left empty rather than citing undated sources. Update: the company post (opened, dated 2023-03-23) names Felix Capital as lead and Philippe Corrot, Mirakl founder and CEO, and Nagi Letaifa, Mirakl Head of Engineering, as additional investors. Only one Mirakl founder is named, so the plural founders is not supported. It calls the round an equity round with no stage, so stage is other. A further search for competitors near 2021 returned only current listing pages (CB Insights, SaaSHub, TrustRadius) and undated vendor blogs, so the competitor list stays empty.
